## Resulting path

The original native basis refresher could inspect a trained-dictionary leaf but had only a fixed release callback, not authenticated dictionary custody or a resizable decoder receipt. At that exact old dictionary guard, this patch adds the one selected synchronous cache-owned reader. The raw/Snappy/LZ4 read body remains byte-identical. There is no generic fallback, new codec/default, logical cut, root/LSN relaxation, global dictionary cache, ordinary-budget subsidy or higher limit.

Before `writerMu`, the original cache maintenance budget admits a private operation scope, fixed MaxResources entry vector, callback/unwind cells and original cleanup record. Under the same writer gate the actual old/new basis Snapshots are bound in order. Native scratch borrows the scope only during that refresh; active/frozen refreshes share this operation's bounded dictionary custody. Original descriptor/catalog/root/state-token/applied-LSN predicates remain unchanged. The scratch and its borrowed authority are cleared on exit; no provider is stored in `nativeEngineVersion`.

For the real inspected dictionary record, the reader uses its exact pinned file and producer ID. `PrepareDictionaryReadDefinitionInto` is a minimal sibling of the existing authenticated preparation kernel: it transfers into the already-admitted caller slot immediately after owner admission, before capture/any later admission callback. Every partial owner is therefore retained even on error, panic or Goexit in the tested later stages. The old return-only provider alone cannot provide this unwind contract and remains unsupported on this new path. Ordinary Acquire/Prepare/Close/ReleaseCapture behavior is preserved; owner size accounting naturally includes the new completion fields.

The same maintenance budget admits all definition/snapshot/metadata/pin stages and input/raw/decoder wrapper. `NewCOWBoundedDecoder` authenticates SHA producer identity and grammar, uses the same typed lease's `ResizeWork`, and preserves frame producer, bounded output and decoder continuation rules. `ReadCOWLeafPageDiagnostic(..., true, ...)` preserves actual shape reinspection, CRC, native source and compact page checks. The caller owns the copied page; the decoder and input/raw aliases are detached before their lease closes. Repeated dictionary IDs reuse one immutable definition only inside this operation. Distinct IDs consume fixed slots and charged owners; full capacity refuses before the next provider effect.

## Off-gate cleanup and original error custody

The prepared DictionaryReadDefinition adopts the SAME Snapshot's existing final cleanup completion receipt. `ClosePreparedRead` does not treat Close acceptance or a nil error as completion: it requires the receipt's actual scalar completion publication, after the original finalizer's aliases and callbacks. A missing/incomplete or failed cleanup retains the same owner, snapshot, bytes, pin and receipts; repeated observation does not retry or refund. This new protocol must not be mixed with the legacy Close/ReleaseCapture protocol.

The scope's deferred transfer is registered before the writer Unlock defer, so it runs after writer unlock, including actual preparation panic/Goexit. It clears the exact before/after borrowed snapshots and transfers its preborn record to the **existing sole semantic cleanup worker**. It does not borrow the exclusive cleanup guard from another goroutine or join that worker while holding flushMu. Those alternatives would respectively conflict with an already-running cleanup or the worker's own subsequent flushMu acquisition. There is no new worker, scheduler or queue.

Successful entries are cleared. Failed entries keep their original owners and individual failures; the scope preserves the first cleanup error without building an unadmitted error chain. Failure returns no completion/refund. The existing worker parks the same record/work, publishes original error/poison/debt and keeps the original checked Close failure. On total success the scope clears cache/provider/vector aliases, detaches the independent lease, and returns the existing final completion. The worker clears record/work aliases before completing it. A scope that performed no provider effect has only accounting to refund and needs no cleanup guard. Checked cache Close already joins the eligible worker frontier before backend/dictionary-store teardown.

Original private-next-cut and captured-basis ownership also survive the selected provider unwind: the existing admission includes fixed caller unwind cells, the original private semantic states are retired after gate unlock, and the captured basis is released by the original owner on normal/error/unwind paths. This does not recover, suppress or replace the panic/Goexit. A cleanup error during unwind is retained on the existing DB owner. No physical lifetime or recovery assertion is weakened.
